title: Christmas Party Photo Booth Ideas: 20 Cheap DIY Backdrops
description: Christmas party photo booth ideas on a budget: 20 DIY backdrops, a prop list, lighting fixes, phone vs rental costs, and office and family versions.
dek: Build it, light it, shoot it, and get the photos to everyone after.
excerpt: Twenty cheap backdrops from tinsel walls to a giant gift box, the lighting rules that fix dark booth photos, gear from a free phone setup to a rented booth, and how guests get their strips.
secondary_keywords: christmas party photo booth ideas diy
simple christmas party photo booth ideas

faq.q: How do you make a cheap photo booth for a Christmas party?
faq.a: Tape a tinsel curtain or wrapping paper to a wall about 6 feet wide, put a lamp just above your phone so it lights faces, and set the phone on a tripod or a stack of books at chest height. Use the camera timer or a Bluetooth remote, and fill a basket with hats, headbands and wrapped empty boxes.

faq.q: What props do you need for a Christmas photo booth?
faq.a: About one big prop per person in the frame, plus spares: Santa and elf hats, antler headbands, scarves and mittens, a giant candy cane, stick-on bows and empty boxes wrapped as presents. Blank speech bubbles with a dry-erase marker are the crowd favorite. Skip anything that hides faces, glitter, and at work, mistletoe.

faq.q: How much does it cost to rent a photo booth for a Christmas party?
faq.a: Thumbtack’s 2026 cost guide puts the national average at $361 to $605, with some companies charging $125 to $200 an hour and packages usually starting at two or three hours. Prints, props and an attendant can change the price, so ask what’s included. For a December weekend, request quotes a few weeks ahead.

faq.q: How do you take photo booth pictures with an iPhone?
faq.a: Mount the iPhone on a tripod at chest height, 6 to 8 feet from where people stand, on the 1x lens. Use the built-in timer (3, 5 or 10 seconds), a Bluetooth shutter remote, or an Apple Watch with the Camera Remote app. A booth mode in a camera app adds a countdown and builds strips automatically.

faq.q: Where should you put a photo booth at a party?
faq.a: Close to where people gather, like the dessert table or the coffee, but out of the main walkway so the line doesn’t block traffic. Avoid spots with a window or lamp behind the backdrop. At an office party, keep it away from the bar and run it hardest in the first hour.
